name: Mobile car detailing business
blurb: Wash, clean and detail cars at the customer's home or workplace, paid per vehicle
title: Mobile Detailing Business: How to Start, Costs and Risks
description: How a mobile detailing or mobile car wash business makes money, the kit you need, who it suits, the water and damage risks, and how to test it cheaply.
h1: How to start a mobile detailing business
answer: A mobile detailing business, sometimes called a mobile car wash, goes to the customer's home or workplace to wash, clean and protect their car, charging per vehicle or per package. It needs less money than a fixed car wash, mainly cleaning products, tools and a vehicle. The catches are long physical days, weather, water and runoff rules, and the risk of damaging paint or interiors.

body: You sell packages: an exterior wash, an interior clean, a full detail, and add-ons such as paint correction, ceramic coatings, pet-hair removal or odour treatment. Regular maintenance washes for busy owners and small fleets bring steady repeat work.
Margin goes to products, water and power, travel between jobs, insurance and equipment. Full details take hours, so the number of cars you can do in a day caps what you earn.

ul: Washing and detailing kit: pressure washer or water tank, vacuum, buckets, microfibre towels, brushes and products for paint, glass, leather and fabric.
A vehicle that can carry water, a generator or power source if clients cannot provide one.
Skill: learn safe washing methods first, and do not offer paint correction or coatings until you have practised on your own car.
Insurance: liability cover, and ask about cover for damage to customers' vehicles while in your care.

Local paperwork: rules differ by country and city. Some places restrict wash water running into storm drains, so a mat or water recovery may be needed; check with your city, and ask about business licences and permits for working on public streets.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: Car enthusiasts who enjoy careful, detailed work
Anyone who rushes or dislikes repetitive tasks
People comfortable working outdoors in heat and cold
People who need steady income through bad-weather months
Good communicators who can upsell honestly
Areas with strict water rules and no way to capture runoff

ul: Damage: swirl marks, burned paint from a polisher or a ruined seat can cost more than the job. Inspect and photograph each car before starting.
Weather cancels outdoor jobs and makes scheduling unpredictable.
Runoff and water use rules can bring fines or block you from some sites.
Price competition from cheap washes; sell care and results, not the lowest price.
Physical strain from kneeling and bending all day.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Detail your own car and two friends' cars with basic kit and time each step.
Check map listings for mobile detailers near you and compare their packages.
Offer three paid washes in your street or workplace car park at a real price.
Ask the property manager of an office or apartment block whether residents could book you on site.
Cost products, fuel and time per car; if a full day earns less than you need, change the packages.
Register the business, get insurance and check local water and parking rules.
Start with two or three clear packages instead of a long menu.
Use a pre-job checklist with photos of existing scratches and damage.
Build a before-and-after gallery and ask each client for a review.
Offer a recurring maintenance plan to turn one-off customers into regulars.

faq.q: What is the difference between a car wash and detailing?
faq.a: A wash cleans the surface. Detailing goes further: deep cleaning the interior, decontaminating and polishing paint, and protecting surfaces. Detailing takes longer and is priced higher.

faq.q: Do I need my own water and power?
faq.a: Not always, but relying on clients' taps and sockets limits where you can work. Many mobile detailers carry a water tank and a power source so they can work in car parks and offices.

faq.q: Can I start mobile detailing part-time?
faq.a: Yes. Evenings and weekends suit many customers who want their car cleaned at home. Start with simple packages and add advanced services once you have the skill.
